<reason>A wins narrowly. B established a genuine protection gap before orders arrive, which A candidly conceded. But A better tested the breadth of B’s proposed duty: targeting a “throwaway brigade” still requires distinguishing harassment infrastructure from anonymous lawful organizing. A explained why the express shield leaves platforms incentivized to suppress disputed networks. B’s closing returned to obvious swatting materials rather than resolving that boundary or justifying the wider obligation.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B argued that an express shield broke the liability asymmetry. A directly replied that preserving a network still requires defending its classification, while disabling it avoids that dispute without corresponding liability for lost lawful reach. This preserved A’s central objection despite B’s strongest safeguard.</best_rebuttal>
